claims.text: The alloy in the controlled comparison is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy is single phase.
The initial and grain-refined CoCrFeMnNi alloy has an FCC structure.
A grain size near or above 10 μm represents the coarse-grained baseline.
Plastic deformation in coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi is dominated by screw dislocations.
Severe plastic deformation can reduce the grain size of single-phase CoCrFeMnNi to the nanocrystalline regime.
Refining CoCrFeMnNi from a coarse-grained state to an ultrafine or nanocrystalline state increases room-temperature strength.
Refining CoCrFeMnNi to an ultrafine-grained state increases hardness.
Grain refinement changes the governing deformation behavior in CoCrFeMnNi.
The grain-refinement-induced mechanism change is specifically a transition from screw-dislocation-mediated plasticity to edge-dislocation-mediated plasticity.
Edge dislocations predominate in ultrafine-grained CoCrFeMnNi.
Activation and predominance of edge dislocations cause the increased hardness and strength of ultrafine-grained CoCrFeMnNi.
Grain refinement is accompanied by evolving local chemical disorder.
Grain size and local chemical disorder jointly modify dislocation-core structures and grain-boundary characteristics.
Hall–Petch-like strengthening in CoCrFeMnNi remains applicable down to roughly 80–100 nm.
At grain sizes of approximately 10–50 nm, grain-boundary sliding becomes the dominant deformation mechanism.
At grain sizes of approximately 10–50 nm, CoCrFeMnNi undergoes inverse Hall–Petch softening.
The nanoscale softening is caused by grain-boundary sliding.

contradictions.description: Inverse Hall–Petch softening and grain-boundary sliding are presented as possibilities ('may' and 'possibility of deviation'), but failure to observe inverse Hall–Petch softening is nevertheless made a mandatory rejection criterion.

The stated validity range ends at approximately 100 nm, whereas the proposed 10–50 nm softening threshold lies outside that range; the falsification rule nonetheless requires behavior at that outside-range threshold.
